Assignment and revocation history is per-user and per-assignment, ordered chronologically, immutable (append-only UserRoleAssignmentEvents), and tenant-isolated
Every history event records who performed it (PerformedByUserId) and why (Reason) - System-sourced events (auto-provisioning) carry no PerformedByUserId

Functionality: If the seeded Employee role is somehow missing from the Roles table, provisioning logs a warning and silently returns rather than throwing - a Link/Replace still succeeds, just without granting the role
API: n/a - not reachable against the seeded database; documented defensive branch

Functionality: Employee-role provisioning and the link mutation happen inside the SAME database transaction and the same SaveChangesAsync call as the link event itself - an audit-write failure rolls back both together
Service: AccountEmployeeLinkService.MutateAsync (single BeginTransactionAsync .. SaveChangesAsync .. CommitAsync wrapping both the link event and the role provisioning)

Functionality: Recording an employment change with a ManagerId provisions the seeded Manager role for that manager's LINKED account - System-sourced, effective today, reason 'Reporting manager assignment' - ONLY if the manager is presently a current (non-superseded, not-yet-ended) manager on at least one EmployeeEmploymentHistory row

Functionality: The Manager role is granted at most once per manager's linked account - a second/third direct report assigned to the same already-Manager-role-holding account does not create a duplicate UserRoles row

A future-dated employment change naming a manager (EffectiveFrom in the future) STILL provisions the Manager role today - EnsureForManagerEmployeeAsync's own 'is currently a manager' probe checks EffectiveTo (or null) >= today, not EffectiveFrom <= today, so a not-yet-effective manager assignment is enough
API: POST /api/employees/{id}/employment-history (ManagerId set, EffectiveFrom in the future)
Service: ManagerRoleProvisioningService.EnsureForManagerEmployeeAsync (x.EffectiveTo == null || x.EffectiveTo >= today - no lower bound against EffectiveFrom)

Functionality: Manager role provisioning is deliberately additive/one-way - there is no code path anywhere that REMOVES the Manager role once a manager's last direct report is reassigned elsewhere (documented in the service's own XML doc comment)
UI: n/a (RoleManagementPage never shows an automatic revoke for Manager)
API: n/a - no removal endpoint reachable for a System-sourced Manager assignment (also blocked by F-RBAC-036's system-role guard)
Service: ManagerRoleProvisioningService (XML doc: 'Role assignment is deliberately additive... never removed here')

Functionality: There is no startup/seed reconciliation job that re-scans all current manager relationships and back-fills missing Manager role assignments - provisioning fires only at the moment an employment-history change is recorded

Functionality: A manager assigned via the LEGACY full-record path (Employee.ReportingManagerId, set through PUT /api/employees/{id}) does NOT trigger Manager-role provisioning - only a POST to the Employment History endpoint does

Functionality: A manager with multiple current direct reports is provisioned the Manager role exactly once, at whichever direct report's employment change is recorded first

Get an account's current link state (Unlinked / Linked / Invalid) plus the latest event id ('revision') used for optimistic concurrency on the next mutation
Get link state by employee id instead of user id (reverse lookup); an unlinked employee reports Unlinked with no user context rather than 404

UI: AccountEmployeeLinksPage employee candidate 'Eligibility' column (Eligible/Ineligible is a display hint only, not itself the enforcement)

Functionality: Linking a user to the SAME employee they are already linked to is rejected the same way as any other already-linked case (Conflict) - re-linking identical state is not a silent no-op
An invalid/nonexistent userId or employeeId on link is reported as NotFound (Account not found / Employee not found) distinctly

UI: AccountEmployeeLinksPage (refreshSelected + loadCandidates both re-run after unlink)

Functionality: Replace atomically swaps the current link for a new employee in ONE call - the old AccountEmployeeCurrentLinks row is removed and a new one added in the same SaveChangesAsync, never leaving the account transiently unlinked

API: POST /api/account-employee-links/users/{userId}/replace (newEmployeeId already linked to another user)

Functionality: Replace to the SAME employee the account is already linked to is rejected as Conflict ('Replacement target must differ')

UI: AccountEmployeeLinksPage textarea (maxLength=500, submit button disabled while blank)

The controller stacks BOTH [HasPermission(View)] and [HasPermission(Manage)] on every mutating action (link/unlink/replace/candidates) - ASP.NET Core's multiple-Authorize-attribute semantics require BOTH to hold (logical AND), so Manage alone (without View) is insufficient
A role holding ONLY AccountEmployeeLink.View (e.g. AccountLinkAuditor, which holds View+ViewHistory but not Manage) can read current state and history but gets 403 on link/unlink/replace/candidates
UI: AccountEmployeeLinksPage 'Eligible employees'/'Link / replace' section hidden entirely for a View-only caller (canManage=false)

A role holding Manage without View cannot exist as a reachable state through the seeded matrix (both AccountLinkAdministrator entries always pair View+Manage) - directly testable only via the CR-66 Page Access Management path
API: POST /api/account-employee-links/users/{userId}/link (a role granted Manage only, via Page Access Management)

Functionality: An unlinked account reports EmployeeIdentity.Status='Unlinked', EmploymentEligibility='NotLinked', and nav items flagged requiresEmployeeIdentity (My Profile, Apply Leave, My Attendance, etc.) are hidden from navigation

EmployeeIdentityResolver reports Conflict ('requires administrator review'), not a crash, when the current-link row is orphaned (its EmployeeId no longer resolves) - mirrors AccountEmployeeLinkService's own Invalid-state handling

The Role Management page's OWN required permission is RoleManagement.AssignmentView, not RoleManagement.View or .Manage - so SuperHR (View+AssignmentView) sees the page, but a hypothetical role holding only RoleManagement.View (with no AssignmentView) would NOT

Existing Tests: Vitest pages/administration/PageAccessManagementPage.test.tsx :: loads paged authorization history with readable permission changes

Service: RoleScopeResolver.AppliesAsync (invoked once per UserRole assignment, not once per user)

Functionality: Accounts + Employee: Accounts holds only Employee.View (tenant-wide, no scope) - combined with the Employee role's self-service permission set, the account gets tenant-wide employee read PLUS its own self-service Leave/Payroll/Separation actions, still as a UNION with no page/permission lost from either role

IT + Employee: IT holds User.View/.Edit and AccountEmployeeLink.View (but not .Manage) - combined with Employee's self-service grants, the account can view/edit User rows and view (not perform) account-employee links, alongside its own self-service actions

Two simultaneous Link attempts for the same never-linked account both racing on a null revision are serialized by the AccountEmployeeCurrentLinks table's own PK/lookup and the transaction wrapping each MutateAsync call - the loser sees the winner's new state on retry and its own attempt is rejected as Conflict ('The account is already linked')

A concurrent Replace racing against another Replace/Unlink on the same account is rejected by the SAME optimistic-revision check as any other mutation - the second caller's stale revision no longer matches the latest event id

Simultaneous duplicate role assignment (same user+role+overlapping period, submitted twice concurrently) leaves exactly one UserRoles row and one Assigned event, resolved by the Serializable-transaction retry loop

A simultaneous assign and revoke targeting the SAME assignment do not corrupt the audit trail - each writes its own event, and the final UserRoles.EffectiveTo reflects whichever transaction committed last, with no partially-written row
